regular_joint_edit.description: Redefine root-owned regular joint geometry, motion family, offsets, angle, flip or lock. Restore timeline in finally and verify after recompute. Use joint_edit for name, suppression, limits and drive values; joint_delete for deletion.

jointOne.description: Guarded reference from inspect in this document/revision; occurrence references retain instance context.

jointTwo.description: Guarded reference from inspect in this document/revision; occurrence references retain instance context.

valueTwo.description: Number in mm (angle in deg), or a dimensionally valid Fusion parameter expression.

motion_link_create.description: Create a native motion link between two root-owned joints, or two different motions of jointOne when jointTwo is omitted. Positive ratio magnitudes use mm for translation and deg for rotation; reversed selects opposite direction. Requires the November 2025+ API; no script fallback.

link.description: Guarded reference from inspect in this document/revision; occurrence references retain instance context.

valueOne.description: Number in mm (angle in deg), or a dimensionally valid Fusion parameter expression.

valueTwo.description: Number in mm (angle in deg), or a dimensionally valid Fusion parameter expression.

motion_link_edit.description: Edit a root-owned motion link ratio, degree-of-freedom pair, direction, name or suppression. Joint membership is immutable; recreate the link to change members. Verify exact joint identities, ratio, flags and health.

link.description: Guarded reference from inspect in this document/revision; occurrence references retain instance context.

motion_link_delete.description: Delete a root-owned motion link under the same transaction/recovery contract.

configuration_inspect.description: Read the loaded Design configuration graph without activation or recompute: ordinary rows, the separate native reserved test row, all supported typed cells including inactive/test cells, exact controlled-source links and current ordinary row. Unreadable fields and unknown/theme/hierarchical/inserted scopes remain explicit incomplete diagnostics. Configuration lifecycle and configured-design model mutations remain disabled pending native recovery/archive gates.

render_scene_inspect.description: Guarded main-thread read of current viewport camera, render settings and up to 32 environments. Optional detached world-mm camera is constructed and read back without viewport assignment. Missing fields return PARTIAL; observationComplete covers only bounded available scope. sceneWitnessComplete and renderQualified remain false. No rendering, workspace activation or scene writes.

occurrence.description: Exact guarded occurrence reference from inspect; every repeated/nested instance is distinct.

exploded_view_plan.description: Read-only source-bound exploded assembly plan. Normalized translation directions in immutable home world/parent/local axes; simultaneous moves within ordered steps. Descendants inherit ancestor translations once, plus own moves. Bounded deterministic sample matrices and exact home reverse endpoint. No native moves, graphics, BOM quantity changes, render/video or storyboard creation. Complete configuration identity required.

occurrence.description: Exact guarded occurrence reference from inspect; every repeated/nested instance is distinct.

exploded_preview_create.description: Create finite copied solid-BRep presentation graphics in the exact active blank unsaved Design proven by a committed current-session new_design result. Regenerates the guarded source plan; leaves source active. Exclusive session lease, no source moves/visibility writes, no model transaction, automatic document close, render or capture. Live capability and native backend qualification are separate from durable operation receipts.

exploded_preview_sample.description: Apply one server-stored absolute sample to exact-owned graphics; preserve active document. Source must remain unchanged. Requires the current controller capability, presentation target, generation and a durable operation ID. Old-session native resources are never rebound.

exploded_preview_show.description: Explicitly activate the exact-owned presentation in Fusion; refuse an intervening foreign active document. No OS foreground, camera change or capture. Requires the current controller capability, presentation target, generation and a durable operation ID. Old-session native resources are never rebound.

exploded_preview_dispose.description: Delete only the exact retained graphics tree and leave the blank document open for caller. Supports a narrowly proven cleanup after unresolved terminal storage without rewriting that history; no global Undo or close. Requires the current controller capability, presentation target, generation and a durable operation ID. Old-session native resources are never rebound.

exploded_preview_inspect.description: Main-thread live preview ownership/geometry/history observation. Cached operation receipts do not establish current graphics liveness. Old-session history remains separately readable through mech_operation_status; no native reference adoption or lifecycle repair is provided here.

efficiency_report.description: Read what makes the design slow to recompute, open and edit, held against the efficiency playbook (skills/fusion-design-efficiency): timeline make-up and health, Position snapshots, Move features, size, repeated definitions made by Paste New, instance-weighted faces, imported history, wires in a parametric design, big sketches, pattern compute options, modeled threads, meshes and empty components. Returns metrics and findings (rule, severity, measured, limit, fix). Read-only and needs no revision digest. It is journaled like bom_export, so a long report on a big design is followed with fusion_mech_operation_status after the relay's 60 s; passes past budgetSeconds are skipped and listed, with complete:false.

budgetSeconds.description: Stop the costly passes after this many seconds (default 120).

computeTiming.description: Also time a full computeAll (slow on big designs; default false).

occurrence.description: Exact guarded occurrence reference from inspect; every repeated/nested instance is distinct.

folder.description: Absolute folder on the PC for frame_00000.png ... (created if missing).

overwrite.description: Replace frames already in folder (default false).

holdSeconds.description: Hold the last pose this long (default 1).

fit.description: Fit the camera to the most exploded state first (default true); false keeps the current view.

glyphs.description: Keep joint, joint origin, sketch, origin and construction glyphs in the images, as the design shows them (default false: they are hidden through Object Visibility for the capture and every switch is put back; the document is not marked modified).

exploded_view_render.description: Render an exploded-view animation for operators: play the same steps as exploded_view_plan on the real occurrences, save one viewport image per frame from a fixed camera (fitted to the most exploded state) with joint, sketch and construction glyphs hidden unless glyphs:true, then revert every move and verify each instance is back home and the document state unchanged. Refuses a design with an uncaptured move. Journaled; follow a long render with fusion_mech_operation_status. Returns the frame folder, timed captions from the steps' titles and instructions, and the ffmpeg line that joins the frames into MP4 (Fusion's API has no video export).

steps.description: Steps in ASSEMBLY order. Each move gives the direction and distance its part comes from (the way it moves out when exploded).

occurrence.description: Exact guarded occurrence reference from inspect; every repeated/nested instance is distinct.

folder.description: Absolute folder on the PC for step_000_after.png (nothing assembled) and step_NNN_before.png / step_NNN_after.png per step (created if missing).

overwrite.description: Replace step images already in folder (default false).

camera.description: auto (default): the isometric view that best shows the parts coming in, framing the moved parts seated and exploded; fit: the current view direction, framing them; current: the view as it is. Always orthographic.

context.description: auto (default): when every moved part sits in one subassembly, everything outside it is moved out of view in every image (and back afterwards); keep: show the whole design.

glyphs.description: Keep joint, joint origin, sketch, origin and construction glyphs in the images, as the design shows them (default false: they are hidden through Object Visibility for the capture and every switch is put back; the document is not marked modified).

exploded_view_stills.description: Step images for assembly instructions, from one fixed orthographic camera, with joint, sketch and construction glyphs hidden unless glyphs:true: per step, in assembly order, the step's parts hovering where they go with earlier steps seated and later steps out of view (before), then seated (after); step_000_after.png shows nothing assembled, so consecutive images differ by exactly the parts that came in. Returns each moved part's box and centre in both images, normalized to the image, and the camera. Moves only the parts whose pose changes, reverts every move, restores the camera and verifies each instance is back home. Up to 64 steps and 2048 moves. Journaled; follow a long run with fusion_mech_operation_status.

render_image.description: Render a photoreal image with Fusion's local renderer: from a standard view fitted to the design (iso by default) or the current view, at a size and quality (25 to 100; 75 by default), in a lighting environment (a Fusion library one or an .hdr/.exr file) and with a backdrop (the environment or a colour), optionally on a transparent background or without the ground. The renderer never draws joint, sketch or construction glyphs; a standard view is fitted with them hidden, so it frames the parts. Waits for the render, then restores the camera, every render setting and the document's scene. The image reaches filename only when the render finished in time; one that runs past timeoutSeconds is cancelled and writes nothing. Journaled: a large, high-quality render runs for minutes, so follow it with fusion_mech_operation_status.

filename.description: Absolute .png or .jpg path on the PC.

quality.description: 25 to 100: 75 is Fusion's Final and 100 its Excellent. Fusion refuses less than 25.

ground.description: Show the ground plane (shadows and reflections); default leaves the document's setting.

environment.description: The environment that lights the scene: a Fusion library environment by name or id, any case (Sharp Highlights, Rim Highlights, Cool Light, Warm Light, Soft Light, Grid Light, Crossroads, Dry lake bed, Field, Photobooth, Plaza, Skylight, Snow Field; render_scene_inspect lists them), or an absolute path to an .hdr or .exr image. Default: the document's own. The document's backdrop stays as it is unless background says otherwise.

background.description: What shows behind the model: "environment" (the environment image) or a colour "#rrggbb". Default: the document's own backdrop. Not with transparent.

timeoutSeconds.description: Default 600. A render still running then is cancelled (its render process is ended) and writes nothing.

cam_tools.description: List the tools of one of Fusion's tool libraries, with diameter, corner radius and flute length in mm: library milling or hole (Fusion's metric samples; milling by default), any sample or local library by its name, or document (the tools this document's CAM already uses). Filter by type, description (a substring) and diameter range. Every reply also lists the libraries cam_job can name.

library.description: milling, hole, document, or a library name from the reply's libraries (Milling Tools (Inch), a local library, ...).

cam_job.description: Make a milling job: a setup on the given bodies, with optional stock (relative_box with offsets, fixed_box with a size, or solid stock bodies) and WCS origin (a stock or model box point, or the model origin); then operations in order: face, adaptive2d, pocket2d, contour2d, drill (cycle drill, peck or chip_break), adaptive, pocket_clearing, contour (3D contour), parallel or scallop, each with a tool from a Fusion library chosen by type, description, flutes and nearest diameter, and optional Fusion parameter overrides by name. 2D operations take faces (contour2d: their outside, inside or all loops; pocket2d and adaptive2d: pocket floors), else the outside of the setup bodies' silhouette or the bodies' pocket floors (upward faces below their top). Drill picks the bodies' holes of the drill's diameter unless holeFaces are given. Generates the toolpaths (an operation Fusion leaves untouched gets one more try) and reports every operation's status (generated, empty, error, outdated, suppressed, not_generated), warnings, errors and machining time. With post, writes G-code through a post from Fusion's library (FANUC, Grbl, HAAS - Next Generation Control, ...) into post.folder, named and numbered post.program; it does not post while an operation lacks a valid toolpath. Opens the Manufacture workspace once if the document has no CAM yet, then returns to the user's workspace and says so. Journaled.

stock.description: relative_box (Fusion's default) takes offsetMm sides/top/bottom; fixed_box takes sizeMm [x, y, z]; solid takes stock bodies.

wcs.description: The work coordinate system's origin: a box point of the stock (stock_point) or of the model (model_point), top center by default (top 1 to 4 are the top corners at x-min y-min, x-max y-min, x-min y-max, x-max y-max), or the model origin. The axes stay the model's.

library.description: milling (default), hole (default for drills), document, or a library name cam_tools lists.

type.description: Tool type as Fusion names it: flat end mill, ball end mill, bull nose end mill, drill, chamfer mill, ...

description.description: A substring of the tool's description, case-insensitive.

faces.description: 2D geometry: contour2d contours these faces' loops; pocket2d and adaptive2d clear these pocket floors. Without faces: the bodies' silhouette, or their pocket floors.

loops.description: contour2d: which loops of each face (or of the silhouette) to contour; outside by default.

cycle.description: drill: Fusion's drilling (G81), deep-drilling (G83) or chip-breaking (G73) cycle.

peckDepthMm.description: Peck depth for cycle peck or chip_break.

program.description: Program name or number, and the file's name (FANUC and HAAS take a number, 1 to 9999).

comment.description: Program comment, written after the program number.

cam_inspect.description: Read the active document's CAM: setups, their operations' toolpath state, warnings and errors, and NC programs.

revision.description: Refuse with stale_revision unless the model is still at this revision (costs the revision digest, about 5 s on a 4,579-occurrence assembly).

target.description: Optional, as for inspect: the active document must be this one, and the model at revision when one is given. The reply carries the current target either way.

scope.description: Full path of the occurrence whose parts to list ("Panel:1", "Cell:1+Panel:1"). Empty or omitted: the root component's.

maxBodies.description: Bodies read per part for its box, breadth first through its children (default 200; a body proxy's box costs about 26 ms on a big assembly). A part whose walk stopped there has boxCapped:true.

assembly_layout.description: Read one scope's parts for planning an assembly order, without changing anything: every visible occurrence directly under the scope occurrence (or the root), each with path, name, component name, grounded, the number of its children and its box (axis-aligned, root space, mm, from its bodies and its children's; null for a part with no bodies), plus the scope component's unsuppressed joints and as-built joints ([partOne, partTwo, "joint"|"asBuilt"], "" for the scope's own geometry) and rigid groups as part paths, frameBodies (bodies of the scope component itself), document and scopeName. Journaled like efficiency_report: the first guarded read after the add-in loads registers every entity of a big assembly and can outlive the relay's 60 s, so follow it with fusion_mech_operation_status. Returns the current target; pass it to ray_cast.

revision.description: Refuse with stale_revision unless the model is still at this revision (costs the revision digest, about 5 s on a 4,579-occurrence assembly).

target.description: From assembly_layout or inspect. The active document must be this one; with revision the model must still be at it. Without revision no digest is computed and the reply's target carries none.

occurrences.description: Full root-context paths of the occurrences the rays are cast against; each ray names its own by index.

rays.description: Rays in root space. Each is cast against each occurrence it names, in that occurrence's own component coordinates; hidden bodies count too. An empty list only checks the target.

length.description: Hits farther than this (mm) are dropped.

budgetSeconds.description: Stop casting after this many seconds (default 30) so the reply comes back inside the relay's 60 s; the reply then has complete:false and answers the first `cast` rays. Send the rest in another call.

ray_cast.description: Cast batches of rays against named occurrences, without changing anything (assembly planning: what a part seats on, what blocks its way in, whether a tool reaches a screw). Each ray is cast against each occurrence it names, in that occurrence's own component coordinates, about a millisecond on a part, where a ray against a big subassembly's component (thousands of bodies) took a quarter of a second. Returns hits: a row per ray answered, [[occurrence index, distance in mm rounded to 0.01], ...], one entry per occurrence the ray meets within length (its nearest hit), nearest first; a ray that starts inside a body meets that body's exit face. Also cast (rays answered, in order), complete, missing (indexes with no occurrence at that path), failed (casts Fusion refused) and seconds. Not journaled: it stops at budgetSeconds or before its reply passes 1 MiB (stopped: budget|reply_bytes) and the caller sends the remaining rays. Requests over the CLI's argument limit (128 KiB) go in several calls.

drawing_create.description: Make a 2D drawing of the active design with Fusion's automatic drawing: sheets laid out by Fusion, each with a base view and its projected views (front, top, right), an optional isometric view, a filled title block and automatic dimensions. The design must be saved to the cloud with no unsaved changes (or pass useSavedVersion); the drawing is a new cloud file next to the design, or in folderId, never in a project's root folder. Fusion picks the views' scale for the sheet size; the API cannot set it. Takes about 30 s for a part. Journaled. Follow with drawing_export.

units.description: mm for iso, in for asme by default.

sheetSize.description: A4 to A0 with iso, A to E with asme; A3 or B by default.

views.description: Base and projected views (default true) and an isometric view beside them (default true).

dimensions.description: Automatic dimension strategy; overall by default, none for views only.

datum.description: Origin for baseline and ordinate dimensions on part sheets.

content.description: Draw every part, or only the visible ones.

sheets.description: Which sheets Fusion makes: the main assembly, subassemblies, one per part (component), sheet metal; levels first or all.

omit.description: Parts left out of part sheets: names containing these comma-separated keywords (Bolt,Screw,Nut,Washer by default) and, with fasteners, any part Fusion recognizes as a fastener.

configuration.description: Configuration name for a configured design; the active one by default.

folderId.description: Cloud folder to put the drawing in; the design's folder by default.

name.description: Name for the drawing file; Fusion's is '<design> Drawing'.

useSavedVersion.description: Draw the last saved version even though the design has unsaved changes.

drawing_export.description: Export a drawing made by drawing_create to PDF, DWG and DXF (absolute paths on the PC), staged and published with byte counts and SHA-256. The first call opens the drawing in Fusion and answers drawing_not_ready (retryable, retryAfterSeconds); call again with a new operationId. Never in the call that opens it: an export sent while Fusion's Edit Auto Dimensions command runs on a newly opened drawing blocks Fusion's main thread for 10 minutes. A later call ends that command if it is running, and exports once the sheets read, Fusion runs no command and the drawing engine is idle and quiet. A drawing opened by someone else is refused (drawing_open_elsewhere). DXF holds the active sheet; with a DXF the reply also gives the scale Fusion chose, read from its dimensions. close:true closes the drawing and the design its open brought in. Journaled.

drawing.description: The drawing's cloud file, as drawing_create returned it.

pdf.description: Absolute .pdf path; one PDF of every sheet unless pdfSheets.

pdfSheets.description: Sheets for the PDF, like "1-3" or "1,4"; every sheet by default.

close.description: Close the drawing in Fusion after exporting, with the design its open brought in when that was not open before and is unmodified, and put the previously active document back (default false).

drawing_status.description: Whether a drawing is open and ready for drawing_export: its sheets read, Fusion's active command, the drawing engine's unfinished commands and how long its log has been quiet, and the sheets with their views. Changes nothing.

drawing.description: The drawing's cloud file, as drawing_create returned it.
